title: Anatomy of a Good Data File
creator: Hank Ratzesberger & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Six CSV files, each broken in exactly one way, each paired with an analysis question it cannot answer, plus a repair mode and a seven-question metadata checklist judged by a six-months-later test.

educational.topic: Anatomy of a Good Data File
learningObjectives: Critique real data files against a usability standard.
Identify the specific omission that makes a given file uninterpretable.
Construct a header row and metadata record that repairs it.
Judge a file against a reader who has no memory of the installation.
prerequisites: Chapter 14: CSV structure, header rows and metadata

keyQuestions: What is the third column of a file with no header?
Can 995 hPa be interpreted without knowing the elevation?
Which of two rows stamped 01:30 came first?
Would this file still be usable to you next spring?
commonMisconceptions: A header row is enough documentation.
Units can be inferred from the magnitude of the numbers.
Local timestamps are fine as long as you know your own time zone.
assessmentOpportunities: Selects 'cannot be determined' correctly and names the missing information.
Repairs a file until the original question becomes answerable.
Passes the six-months-later test with a file of their own design.
